title: The mill at Muileann shean
summary: A mill is raised on the northern road at Muileann shean to grind grain for the carriers crossing the pass; the miller pays the Hall in grain and the rìgh's toll in flour, and a town grows round the mill within two generations.

title: Catrìona Ghlic dies at a hundred and twenty-two
summary: Catrìona Ghlic, who mended the breach her father Iain Garbh's war had opened, dies at Dùn dhearg. Her son takes the hall at ninety-two, the first of eleven rulers the later king-list will give only by name and order.

title: The Hall's own roll for the same years
summary: For the span the king-list gives eleven rulers, the Hall's spoken roll gives only five Keepers, a mountain's years running longer than a lowland's, as every teller of the Fire already knows.

title: The last of the long years in the ruling line
summary: The last ruler of the house of Ìomhar and Goraidh to carry any of the long years in his blood dies at a hundred years old, an age that was a boy's age in his grandmother's grandmother's day. After him the line ages and dies at the pace of any household on the island.

title: Tormod mac Iain born to the house of Tormod
summary: Tormod is born at Dùn dhearg, a younger son of a house that has held no great office in the hall for three generations. His father Iain keeps a stretch of the crown granaries, and the boy grows up among grain-tallies.

title: Tormod sent east to Muileann chiar
summary: A passing stag-teacher's tale of letters that can hold a teaching without a teacher fixes itself in the fifteen-year-old Tormod's mind. His father, a younger son's post being cheaper found elsewhere than at home, sends him east to Muileann chiar to learn the stag-letters.

title: Tormod's first written leaf
summary: In his second summer at Muileann chiar, Tormod writes his first whole leaf, a grain-debt tally copied twice over from an old woman's spoken account. He keeps it inside his shirt a full year, the oldest surviving thing in his own hand.

title: Tormod returns to the granaries
summary: After four years at Muileann chiar, Tormod comes home to Dùn dhearg and his father's trade of the granaries, carrying unspoken a want to write down a thing that would outlast every mouth that had ever spoken it.

title: Ealasaid Chiar takes the hall
summary: Ealasaid Chiar, granddaughter of the ninth of the eleven, takes the hall at Dùn dhearg at twenty-nine, out of patience with hearing her own house's roll given a different order at every telling.

title: Ealasaid Chiar sets Tormod to the writing
summary: Ealasaid Chiar hears of a granary clerk who can set a thing down in marks and have it read back the same way twice, and sets Tormod Scrìobhaiche, now fifty-nine, to write down every ruler the reciters can name, in order, freed of all other duty.

title: The reciters disagree
summary: Questioning the hall's reciters in turn, Tormod finds them certain and contradictory: a mother's name given two ways, a reign given nine years by one mouth and eleven by another, three rulers set in different orders by a southern reciter than by the hall's own.

title: Ealasaid Chiar bids the doubt be written too
summary: Told of the disagreements, Ealasaid Chiar orders Tormod to set down the sure thing where he has it and the doubt where he has that, rather than hide the roll's own uncertainty from those who could not otherwise judge it.

title: Tormod's roll finished
summary: After six years' careful writing, reading each page back to whoever gave it before counting it done, Tormod brings Ealasaid Chiar the finished roll from Goraidh Mòr to herself, with three disputed places marked and left unresolved.

title: Death of Tormod Scrìobhaiche
summary: Tormod Scrìobhaiche dies at seventy in the clerk's room off the hall at Dùn dhearg, a half-begun copy of the disputed reign still under his hand. Ealasaid Chiar names the room, ever after, Tormod's room.

title: The Hall shamed into writing its own roll
summary: Word of the written king-list reaches the blind Keeper on the mountain, who sits three days in silence and then tells the Hall's own reciters that a Hall out-remembered by a rìgh's clerk has no one to blame but itself.

title: Cairistìona reads the cord for the scribes
summary: Cairistìona nan Snaidhm, last of Sìne's line who can read a knot without letters, comes to the Hall and unties the cord of the heirs knot by knot over two days, naming each heir aloud so a young scribe can set the roll down in the new marks.

title: The cord coiled in its chest
summary: The last of the cord's seven hundred and twelve knots comes free, and Cairistìona coils it in the old way and lays it in the chest the Hall has made for it, telling the scribe that after her no hand living will be able to make it speak.
